Deals rotate, so each session starts from an angle and a half the others didn't get. Work from that copy: read whole and as stored, this file pulls every session toward the same shape.

how_to_read: 1. Deal first: python3 <SKILL>/scripts/deal.py snow-globe.metadump.json, then read the dealt copy it names for every step below (write-backs go to this file).
2. Read the head: the first 35 lines hold manifest, essence and routing (Read limit=35, or jq '{manifest, essence, routing}' snow-globe.metadump.json).
3. Pick the route for your job and run its jq: jq '<routing[i].jq>' snow-globe.metadump.json
4. Also pull the anti-keywords and review prompts (checks) for your scope: jq '.anti_keywords, .checks' snow-globe.metadump.json
5. Look up any term (lowercase): jq '.index["<term>"]' snow-globe.metadump.json  -> hits give id + path; not_meant lists senses to avoid.
6. Grep works too: every entry is one line, so grep -n '<word>' snow-globe.metadump.json returns whole entries.

7. When you have built something that renders, look at it before you finish: python3 <SKILL>/scripts/look.py <your file.html> screenshots it at desktop and phone widths, then plays it (clicks, types, slides, drags and tabs through everything) and lists what breaks along the way and what the page said. Fix what it lists, read its sheet, and look again.

essence.one_sentence: A snow globe is a small weather system you can time: the liquid holds the glitter up long enough that the settle, not the shake, is the part people watch.
essence.summary: Clear water dome, miniature scene, glitter that hangs and drifts, a lens and a clock in one sealed object.

llm_brief.text:
On the table, mixed: the user's words, "snow globe". Specifics with values: a vendor's starting point of about 1 part glycerin to 3 parts water by volume (researched); a small jar of about 2 tablespoons of glycerin with a gap left at the top; 1 to 2 teaspoons of fine glitter per two cups of liquid; plain water drops glitter within seconds, a glycerin-thickened fill holds it several seconds to half a minute; a 1 to 3 mix slows the fall about three times, by a vendor's own Stokes estimate. Lens: a water-filled glass sphere magnifies a marble behind it in air and loses most of its power when submerged in a water dish. Deep cuts: early globes used white semolina flakes in glycol water, and the first one held a small basilica replica; a glass ball held before a telephoto lens renders the whole scene inside it as a fish-eye. Words people use: snow globe, waterglobe, snowstorm, snowdome, Schneekugel, flitter for the particles.
Ways in, side by side: the classic souvenir dome, a heavy dome on a base with one scene and white glitter. A scene-only dome with no base, the scene as the subject, seen through a strong curve. An abstract globe where the falling particles are the subject. A single-figure bubble of water with sparse flakes. A paperweight with suspended particles and a slow tilt stirring a few. A close-up of one dome filling the frame. A shelf in a room with the dome small among other objects. A single hard shake with a long settle. A still picture of a settling globe.
Dials: flake count, from a few that hang to a dense cloud that hides the scene; settle, from a few seconds to a long drift; magnification, from strong to faint and near true size; liquid, from clear to cool blue to amber; base, from heavy black ceramic to plain or none; shake, from one hard shake to a slow tilt.
Worn paths: the usual move is a snowy village in a dome; fresher: a single scene such as rooftops from below, or a hand holding the ball. The usual move is snow falling through air; fresher: flakes that hang in the liquid and tumble. The usual move is a globe of the Earth; fresher: a water-filled dome with a curved highlight. The usual move is a cup of soup or a dry dome; fresher: clear water slightly thickened.
Open: the medium (web page, still image, 3D model, print) and the scene subject are not stated. The watched clip's timings are sampled at an assumed 10 fps, and its fall times are not measured. Each reading lists what it includes, so the consumer picks or combines.

ak-empty-glass-ball.text: A clear sphere with nothing inside reads as a glass ball, not a snow globe.

ak-bubble-no-scene.instead: a sealed dome of liquid with a miniature scene inside, standing on a base, with flakes falling through it
ak-bubble-no-scene.text: A bubble holding no scene drops the dome, base and scene that make the object.

ak-flat-globe.text: A flat circle has no glass, so no refraction or highlight reads as a dome.

ak-clipart-snowman.text: A flat cartoon figure looks pasted in; the figure should sit behind water and glass.

ak-dry-dome.instead: a dome filled with clear liquid, the flakes drifting through it slowly

ak-air-snow.instead: flakes that hang in the liquid and drift down slowly, or tumble and settle when the globe is shaken
ak-air-snow.text: Snow in open air falls and vanishes; in a snow globe the flakes live in the liquid.

ak-snow-globe-weather-map.instead: a sealed water-filled dome with a miniature scene

ak-snow-ground.instead: glitter or flakes suspended in liquid that fall after a shake

request._about: The user's words, verbatim. Nothing is glossed here.

p-snow-globe.text: The whole request is: a snow globe. No medium, size, scene, style or constraint is stated.

specifics._about: Liquid and glitter rates for a snow globe, from two fetched craft and chemistry guides. Glitter fill and glycerin ratio are sourced; fall time is sourced only as a vague range. No particle count and no haze-clearing time were found in any fetched page, so both stay open.

sp-glitter-fill.text: For about two cups of 1 to 3 liquid, a vendor recipe uses one to two teaspoons of fine glitter, a small amount rather than a heap.
sp-glitter-fill.quote: 1–2 teaspoons of fine plastic glitter, or a mix of fine and chunky
behaviors: A light dusting of fine glitter reads as soft snow
Pour off some liquid and add water rather than adding more glitter

sp-glycerin-ratio.text: Vendor and craft guides start from about 1 part glycerin to 3 parts water by volume, and a small jar takes a few tablespoons.
sp-glycerin-ratio.quote: Start with 1 part glycerin to 3 parts water by volume, for example ½ cup glycerin to 1½ cups water.
behaviors: Test-shake before sealing and adjust toward more or less glycerin
The guide's ratio is a starting point, not a tested standard
A small jar globe takes about 2 tablespoons of glycerin, with a gap left at the top so the lid does not push liquid out
A few drops or a teaspoon or two per cup barely changes the thickness, so many globes still snow fast

sp-fall-time.text: Glycerin decides whether the snow lasts a few seconds or about half a minute; plain water drops glitter within seconds.
sp-fall-time.quote: how much glycerin you add decides whether your globe snows for three seconds or for half a minute.
behaviors: Plain water: glitter settles in a few seconds after a shake
Glycerin-thickened fill: several seconds to half a minute, depending on the mix
A 1 to 3 glycerin mix slows the fall about three times compared with plain water, by the guide's own Stokes estimate; a relative cue, not an absolute speed

motion_and_optics._about: How the particles fall and settle, what a shake does, how the dome bends the scene, and what makes water and glass read as real. Measured timings come from the watched clip (frame-diff, sampled at an assumed 10 fps) and are cited by id. The rest is reasoning from the clip and the scraped optics pages, with illustrative spreads where no source gives a number.

options._about: options, not requirements: the dome's clarity is a decision point

opt-dome-clear-strong.text: A clear glass dome with the scene visibly enlarged and curved edges.

opt-dome-faint-soft.text: A faint dome with little magnification, so the scene reads near its true size.

opt-shake-pointer-drag.text: The viewer drags the dome sideways or up and down. The release velocity sets the shake strength: a hard flick churns the whole dome and a slow drag stirs only a few flakes. Works with a mouse or a finger.
behaviors: A fast release churns the whole volume, as in mo-shake-hard
A slow drag lifts a few flakes that float and settle, as in mo-shake-gentle-tilt

opt-shake-button.text: A button plays one fixed shake and then the settle, the same every time. The page sets the impulse and the settle timing from the clip's measured bursts and the frame-diff quiet point, so the replay is repeatable.
behaviors: Every press gives the same churn and the same settle
Repeatable, so a viewer can compare the settle from one shake to the next

opt-shake-device-motion.text: The page reads the phone's motion sensors and shakes the dome when the device is shaken. Needs the device-motion permission on iOS and does nothing on a desktop with no sensor, so pair it with another route.
behaviors: A real shake of the phone drives the strength
Without a sensor the route is silent, so a second route is needed

opt-shake-tilt.text: A slider or the device tilt sets an angle. A small angle stirs a few flakes that keep floating, and a large angle churns the dome, as in the gentle-tilt reading.
behaviors: A small angle lifts few flakes and the scene stays clear
A large angle sends a cloud through the lower dome

vm-media.text: 32 s clip of a bulb-shaped snow globe being shaken by hand, then left to settle. Measured duration 00:00:31.604.

vs-shake-timing.text: Clip timeline: motion bursts at 6.4-6.8 s, 7.6-8.8 s and 10.7-11.1 s, then a hold to 16 s.

fr-00-00-00.text: Bulb-shaped globe on a black base, upright and still, with the scene small in the middle.

fr-00-00-07.text: A hand still holds the black cap while the globe is tilted; a dense white cloud fills the lower dome around the dark block.

fr-00-00-14.text: Fine and chunky white glitter hangs through the whole dome at close range; the Ferris wheel, spire and gold base show through the haze.

fr-00-00-24.text: The haze has thinned: the top of the dome is clearer, particles rest on the top of the dark block and the gold pedestal, and some still hang in the lower half.

sp-glitter-fall.text: Fine glitter drifts down slowly in a thickened liquid; chunky pieces drop quickly and can clump.
behaviors: Fine glitter floats gently and looks like soft snow
Chunky glitter sinks quickly and can clump
A glycol mix makes the snow fall more slowly
White particles rise into a cloud around the dark block
Fine and chunky flakes hang together in the haze
The top of the dome clears before the lower half
signals: clearing at the top of the dome

sp-decision-dome-scale.text: A clear dome with strong magnification versus a faint dome with little distortion; tabletop size versus display size.
behaviors: A clear dome shows the scene larger and bends it at the edge
A faint dome keeps the scene near true size
A tabletop globe reads as a souvenir; a large display globe gives the flakes more room to fall
signals: strong bend at the rim of the glass

lens-magnify.text: A water-filled glass globe magnifies a marble sitting behind it, in air.
behaviors: The marble inside the globe looks larger than the reference marble on the lab jack
The bending happens at the glass and water boundaries, not in the bulk of the water
The scene looks larger through a dome that is surrounded by air
lens-magnify.principle: The sphere is a lens because its curved boundaries bend light; the water is what makes the bend strong.
signals: bright patch on the glass at the sides
the scene appears enlarged through the glass
the far side looks smaller when the globe sits in water

lens-submerged.text: Submerged in a water dish, the globe loses most of its power and the marble looks slightly smaller.
behaviors: Water on both sides of the glass closes the refractive index gap, so the sphere almost stops bending light
The lesson: lensing needs index contrast at each boundary, not only a curved shape
lens-submerged.principle: Shape alone does not make a lens. The index step at each surface does the bending.

lens-water-reads-real.term: how the water reads as real
lens-water-reads-real.visual_read: Top panel: clear glass globe on a black ring, a water-filled glass dish with a visible water line, the marble magnified inside the globe. Bottom: the globe pressed into the dish, its outline nearly vanishes against the water.
lens-water-reads-real.principle: Realism here is clarity and distortion: the water is read by the image it bends, and by the surface line where it meets air.

sc-ball-optics.term: how a glass ball renders the scene

heading_path: How to Create Glass Ball Landscapes – 6 Techniques

sc-ball-optics.text: A glass ball held in front of a telephoto lens shows the whole scene inside it as a fish-eye-like image, framed by the ball's edge.
behaviors: A telephoto lens makes the scene inside the ball read as fish-eye
Closer framing emphasises the scene inside and cuts the ball's edges
A centred crop hides the top and bottom of the scene
sc-ball-optics.principle: The ball itself is the lens: the composition is decided by what sits inside it, not by the outside frame.
signals: curved edge of the ball visible

heading_path: How to Create Glass Ball Landscapes – 6 Techniques

sc-ball-sun-and-focus.text: Focus is set on the scene inside the ball, not the outside; the ball magnifies sunlight.
properties: manual focus on the inside scene
behaviors: Around f/4 keeps the ball sharp and the outside blurred
The glass ball acts as a magnifying glass for sunlight and can burn you or your property
sc-ball-sun-and-focus.principle: The sphere is a magnifier and a focusing element, so light and focus both pass through it.

mo-shake-hard.text: One hard shake churns the whole dome, then the particles keep moving and settle slowly. Measured motion bursts in the clip run from 6.4 s to 11.9 s, then hold.
behaviors: Measured motion bursts: 6.4 to 6.8 s, 7.6 to 8.8 s, 10.7 to 11.1 s
The frame-diff is low from 11.9 s to 16.0 s, so the settle is quiet by then
The hand leaves the frame near 7.5 s, so motion after that mixes hand and particles
mo-shake-hard.principle: One hard impulse puts the whole volume of water in motion, and the water then damps it over a long time.

mo-shake-gentle-tilt.text: The other reading: a slow tilt stirs a few particles, which keep floating without filling the dome. The scene stays clear.
behaviors: The tilt gives the water less impulse, so the cloud never fills the lower dome
Floating particles drift and settle in a slow, uneven drift
mo-shake-gentle-tilt.principle: A small angle gives less impulse, so the glitter stays suspended and settles gently rather than in a storm.

mo-still-reading.term: still picture of a settling globe
mo-still-reading.text: A single upright frame where the settle shows as haze and flake heights, with no motion to read.
behaviors: Haze is densest near the base and thins toward the top
Flakes hang at several heights, some resting on the base
mo-still-reading.principle: A frozen frame keeps the settle as a gradient and a spread of heights.
signals: haze gradient from base to top

mo-shake-input.term: how a page takes a shake
aliases: how the user shakes the dome
mo-shake-input.text: A page that shows a shaken or tilted dome needs a way to take the shake. Each route feeds the same settle, so the choice changes how the viewer feels the shake.
signals: the settle starts when the shake ends

scene_and_base._about: What sits inside the dome, the base, and the liquid and glitter colours. Subjects are a pool labeled by reading (common, unusual, abstract); no one subject is the default. Colours are several far-apart palettes, each with what it does.

options._about: options, not requirements: builder choices where nothing decides it

sb-colour-warm.term: warm amber liquid with gold glitter
sb-colour-warm.text: Amber or brown water with gold flakes: a warm, late-evening read. The brown photo sample (#351207 at 20%) sits near it.
sb-colour-warm.principle: Warmth in the liquid replaces the cold cast; the scene must still read clearly against it.

sb-subject-abstract.term: abstract subject: no figure, a single form
sb-subject-abstract.text: A single sculptural form or folded shape with no figure, so the water and flakes become the subject.
sb-subject-abstract.principle: Use when the dome itself should be the subject.

sb-colour-cold.term: deep blue water with white glitter
sb-colour-cold.text: Blue-tinted water with white or silver flakes: a cold, night-like read that leaves the models unchanged.
behaviors: Blue water gives a cold cast without changing the models
Silver flakes catch the light as they fall
sb-colour-cold.principle: The blue carries the cold; the flakes carry the motion.
signals: white specks in the lower chamber

sb-colour-clear.text: Uncoloured water with fine white flakes: the neutral read, where the glass and the highlight do the work.
behaviors: A bright window highlight makes the dome read as glass before any colour does
Uncoloured water pushes the eye to the scene
sb-colour-clear.principle: With no tint, the lens and the flakes carry the whole image.
signals: no colour cast in the liquid
a hard highlight on the dome

vs-scene-subjects.text: A gold spire and a red-and-gold Ferris wheel stand on a dark brown block, over a gold pedestal.

sp-exemplars-art.text: LigoranoReese restage twenty art movements as laser-cut, laminated globes, with typography and colour as the scene.
behaviors: The movement's look is carried by type and colour instead of figurines
Each globe is signed and dated by the artists
sp-exemplars-art.contribution: Shows that the dome can hold graphic content instead of a miniature scene.

sp-decision-subject.term: scene or particles as the subject
sp-decision-subject.text: A rich scene with few flakes versus an open-looking scene with many falling flakes.
behaviors: A detailed scene with a few flakes keeps the figure as the subject
Many flakes in a plain scene make the fall the subject
signals: the figure is the focal point

sc-ball-subjects-common.rung: the snow globe as a form
sc-ball-subjects-common.text: Typical subjects are open, minimal landscapes with one clear element.
behaviors: A lone tree reads clearly inside a small sphere
Beach and desert scenes stay minimal, so the ball reads as an accent

sc-ball-subjects-unusual.term: unusual scene subjects inside a ball

heading_path: How to Create Glass Ball Landscapes – 6 Techniques

sc-ball-subjects-unusual.rung: the snow globe as a form
sc-ball-subjects-unusual.text: Less expected subjects the page shows: city rooftops, street-level views, and a hand-held ball.
behaviors: Ground-level placement fills half the frame with ground unless the ball sits on a rise
A hand holding the ball is the human element and keeps the background clean
sc-ball-subjects-unusual.principle: Ordinary surfaces such as leaves, puddles and hands can become the scene's frame.
signals: a hand or a rooftop line in frame

w-inside.text: A miniature scene, often a model of a town, landscape or figure; early globes held a ceramic figure or tableau on a black base.
properties: model of a building or town
behaviors: The scene is the subject; the falling snow frames it
A model of a real building ties the globe to a place, as with the first Perzy globe
The base must be heavy enough to hold the globe upright
w-inside.principle: Pick a scene the dome can frame: one figure or building, not a crowd.
signals: one clear element in the middle of the dome

sb-base.text: The base carries the colour while the water stays neutral. The clip's globe is bulb-shaped, sitting on a plain base.

object_anatomy._about: Parts of a snow globe and what makes it read as one. Facets build on the researched parts, names and classic-versus-modern entries; the reading of how they fit together is inferred. Options are labeled readings, not defaults.

options._about: options, not requirements: readings of the object the consumer can pick from. None is the default.

oa-opt-classic.text: Heavy glass dome on a sturdy base with one small scene and white flakes.

oa-opt-scene-only.text: No base or a flat one; the scene fills the dome and is the whole subject.

oa-opt-abstract.text: The falling particles are the subject; no figure, only colour and shape inside the water.

oa-opt-bubble.text: A sealed water bubble holding one figure, no base, sparse flakes.

oa-opt-paperweight.text: Glass with suspended particles and no scene; closer to a paperweight than a snow globe.

w-names.text: The object is also called a waterglobe, snowstorm or snowdome; the particles are called flitter.
behaviors: Each name points at a different emphasis: the water, the weather effect, or the dome
w-names.principle: Use snowdome or waterglobe as search terms; flitter names the particles themselves.

w-classic-modern.text: Classic globes had a heavy lead-glass dome on a ceramic base; modern ones use thinner glass or white plastic and add motors, lights and music boxes.
properties: classic: heavy lead glass, ceramic figure, black ceramic base
modern: plastic dome, lighter base, music box, motor, internal light
behaviors: A classic globe is heavy and sits still; a modern one may shake itself, so no shaking is needed
Glycerol in the water slowed the flakes; motor globes move the snow without it
w-classic-modern.principle: Classic reads as a heirloom souvenir; modern reads as a gadget.

p-dome.text: A transparent sphere, traditionally glass; modern domes are often plastic or acrylic.
behaviors: A plastic dome is lighter and scratch-proof, so it reads as a toy more than a glass heirloom
A glass dome fused to the base reads as a higher-quality piece
The scene looks larger through the curved front of the glass
Bright reflective patches sit on the glass beside the scene
The lower dome holds the most particles
p-dome.principle: The dome is the material cue: glass for heirloom, plastic for play.
signals: bright patch of reflected light on the front
dark cap or seam at the join
bright patches on the glass at the sides

p-liquid.text: Water mixed with glycerin or glycol, thick enough that the particles drift instead of dropping.
behaviors: The thicker mix makes flakes drift down slowly after a shake
Plain thin water lets flakes drop fast, which reads as sand, not snow
p-liquid.principle: Viscosity sets the fall: slow drift is what makes it read as snowfall.
signals: haze that hangs for seconds after a shake

p-flakes.text: Glitter, mica or plastic flakes that churn up on a shake and fall slowly through the water.
behaviors: After a shake the flakes rise and then fall, not in a single pour
Flakes that stay suspended and never settle read as a snow storm in a jar, not a snow globe
Holographic glitter reflects light in rainbow colours
p-flakes.principle: The snow is the motion: it must rise, drift and settle.
signals: flakes still falling after several seconds
flakes still falling several seconds after a shake
uniform white haze that never clears

p-souvenir.text: Started as hand-made souvenirs, then mass-produced; now a collectible and a kitsch gift form.
behaviors: Hand-made pieces are the collectible end; mass-made ones read as gift-shop kitsch
Tourist scenes and holiday themes are the common subjects
A photographed ball reads as a snow globe when the scene is set in its base
p-souvenir.principle: The form is a memento: it shows a place, a holiday or a keepsake.

sp-origin-liquid.text: Early globes used white semolina flakes and glycol-thickened water; the first one held a small basilica replica.
behaviors: Semolina soaked and floated slowly to the base
The first globe was a miniature diorama on a painted base
signals: flakes drifting slowly to the floor of the glass

w-parts.text: A transparent sphere enclosing a miniature scene, with water as the medium the snow falls through.
behaviors: The sphere holds the water, so the water is part of the object, not a separate fill
Shaking churns the white particles up; they then fall slowly through the water
The dome seals the scene and liquid together
The base carries the weight that keeps the sphere upright
w-parts.principle: The snow only reads as snow because the water is what it falls through.

oa-identity.term: what makes it read as a snow globe
oa-identity.text: Four things together: a sealed water-filled dome, a scene on a base, flakes that fall after a shake, and the glass lens effect.
behaviors: Remove the water and it reads as a paperweight
Remove the falling flakes and it reads as a glass ball with a scene
oa-identity.principle: A snow globe needs the water, the scene and the falling snow together; any one missing changes its name.
signals: flakes still falling several seconds after a shake
scene standing on a base under water

mb-composition.term: composition of a snow globe shot
mb-composition.text: One sphere, centred, with its base under it, against a plain or softly blurred background.
behaviors: A blurred window or tree lights behind the globe carry the season without competing with the scene inside
A studio cutout on white reads as a product, with no context to show scale
mb-composition.principle: The sphere is the picture; the backdrop only sets the mood.

mb-glass.text: Clear or faintly tinted glass with a hard window highlight; in sphere photos the scene behind the glass inverts.
behaviors: A bright window reflection on the dome marks it as glass before any text or base is visible
A sphere held against the sky shows the horizon upside down inside it
mb-glass.principle: The glass is what makes a landscape readable as a globe: it bends the view.

mb-liquid-particles.text: Water with fine white or silver flakes that hang, drift and settle in the lower chamber.
properties: water tint from clear to blue
behaviors: Flakes sit in the low chamber after a shake, leaving the upper glass clear
A blue-tinted water gives the scene a cold cast without changing the models
mb-liquid-particles.principle: The motion is the snow: particles settle slowly and never stop on the subject.

mb-base-in-context.text: The base carries the season colour (red, green, gold, cream) while the water stays neutral.
behaviors: A red-trimmed base reads as Christmas before the scene inside is resolved
A black ribbed base against white makes the glass the only lit form
mb-base-in-context.principle: Colour sits in the base and props; the water stays clear or cold.
